questions.question: Which Django class is the usual base class for declaring a database-backed model?
questions.explanation: A subclass of models.Model declares fields and relationships managed by the ORM.

questions.question: Which command generates migration files from changes in Django models?
questions.explanation: makemigrations creates migration files. migrate applies the pending migrations to a database.

questions.question: Which path converter in path('orders/<int:order_id>/', view) controls the Python type passed to view for order_id?
questions.explanation: The int path converter matches decimal digits and passes the converted value as an integer.

questions.question: Which queryset call fetches a single Product by primary key and raises Product.DoesNotExist if none matches?
questions.explanation: get returns exactly one matching object and raises the model's DoesNotExist exception for no matches.

questions.question: Starting from an unevaluated, ordinary queryset qs, which operations normally evaluate it? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Building a list or requesting length evaluates the queryset. filter and order_by build new querysets lazily.

questions.question: A loop lists books and accesses each book.author, a ForeignKey. Which queryset change can fetch each author using the same SQL query?
questions.explanation: select_related joins the single-valued relation in the main SQL query. prefetch_related generally runs a separate query.

questions.question: A list of books displays each book's many-to-many tags. Which method can load those tags in batches before the loop?
questions.explanation: prefetch_related loads related objects in additional queries and attaches them to the corresponding instances in Python.

questions.question: Which Django shortcut returns a model object and raises Http404 when no matching object exists?
questions.explanation: get_object_or_404 performs a lookup and translates the missing-object case into an HTTP 404.

questions.question: A view creates an invoice and its line items in the same database. Which construct rolls back those writes if an exception leaves the block?
questions.explanation: transaction.atomic defines an atomic database block. An exception propagating out rolls back its changes.

questions.question: A bound Django Form is validated and form.is_valid() returns True. Which statements apply? Select all that apply.

options.a: The form automatically inserts a database row
options.b: Validated values are available through form.cleaned_data
options.c: request.POST is replaced with the cleaned values
options.d: A valid IntegerField value is normalized to a Python int

questions.explanation: A validated form exposes cleaned Python values. Validation does not replace request.POST or persist a row.

questions.question: Which tag should appear inside a same-site Django template form using method='post' and Django's normal CSRF protection?
questions.explanation: The csrf_token tag renders a hidden token that Django can validate when the form is submitted.

questions.question: Which setting lists trusted host or domain names against which Django validates the HTTP Host header?
questions.explanation: ALLOWED_HOSTS defines acceptable hosts for Django's Host header validation.

questions.question: Which ORM expression updates a stored counter relative to its database value in a single UPDATE statement?

options.a: Read the row, add 1 in Python, then call save()

questions.explanation: An F expression refers to the column value and lets the database perform the increment.

questions.question: A developer changes a path but keeps its URL pattern name. Which function can build the updated path from the name?
questions.explanation: reverse uses the configured URL patterns to construct a path from a route name and optional arguments.

questions.question: Which are appropriate uses for Django middleware? Select all that apply.

options.a: Add a request ID to incoming requests
options.b: Declare a model field for invoices
options.c: Add a common header to outgoing responses

questions.explanation: Middleware can wrap request and response handling, making it suitable for cross-cutting HTTP behavior.

questions.question: An order list needs an item count on each returned Order object. Which queryset operation adds that per-order value?
questions.explanation: annotate adds a value to each result. aggregate returns a summary over the queryset as a whole.

questions.question: What does a ForeignKey with on_delete=models.CASCADE normally do when Django deletes the referenced object?

options.a: It sets the referencing field to an empty string
options.b: It preserves all referencing objects with their original foreign keys
options.d: It deletes the referencing objects as part of the cascade

questions.explanation: Django follows CASCADE relationships during deletion and includes the dependent objects in the operation.

questions.question: Which built-in test helper can issue an in-process request to a Django view using its URL path?
questions.explanation: Django's test client exercises URL routing and request processing without starting an external web server.

questions.question: A ModelForm must build an instance so the view can set its owner before the first database write. Which call returns the instance without saving it?
questions.explanation: On a valid ModelForm, save(commit=False) returns the instance without saving it.

questions.question: Which queryset methods can answer the stated question without fetching every full model instance into Python? Select all that apply.

options.a: len(qs) for counting an unevaluated queryset without loading instances
options.b: qs.exists() to check whether there is a match
options.c: list(qs) to check for a match without loading results

questions.explanation: exists and count can issue focused database queries. len and list evaluate an unevaluated model queryset into results.
